_README: Committed baseline for the agent memory verification suite.
Each entry is {"min": n} or {"max": n}. A bound of null means the number
has NEVER been measured; that is reported as a FAILURE, not tolerated, and
the failure message prints the JSON to paste back here. A number nobody has
looked at must not read as a pass — that is the defect this whole change
`source` records where a bound came from, so a modelled figure can never be
contract  - restates an assertion the suite already makes elsewhere.
invariant - follows from the production code, not from a measurement.
measured  - observed on a real run; `recorded_at` names that run.
unrecorded- bound is null; the next real run must record it.

recall_pct.note: test_a_capture_recall.py::test_recall_aggregate already asserts recall == 1.0. Restated here so all three headline numbers are gated in one place.

precision_pct.note: test_b_precision_junk.py::test_junk_aggregate already asserts zero junk across ALL_LABELED. 100% precision is the same statement as a junk count of 0.

non_canonical_rate_pct.note: Every production write path normalises the category before it reaches the column - memory_service.py:536, memory_extractor.py:872 and :1131, agent_reflection.py:168. A row whose stored value is not canonical for its brain means a path bypassed normalize_category, which is a structural defect independent of extraction quality.

unlabeled_rate_pct.note: No run has ever produced this number and it cannot be derived from the code: it depends on how often the real extractor picks the catch-all bucket. Guessing a ceiling here would be a modelled figure wearing a measured figure's clothes. The first run that completes will fail with the measured value and the exact line to paste; record it, commit it, and this becomes a real ratchet.
